s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Lesions symmetrically distributed and ranging from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 40s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions appeared on cheeks 2 years earlier and gradually coalesced
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

raw.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Lesions symmetrically distributed and ranging from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 40s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions appeared on cheeks 2 years earlier and gradually coalesced
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple asymptomatic, round, hypopigmented macules on the face and neck, with no hair growth at the site of the lesions and previous unsuccessful treatment for tinea versicolor, is most consistent with idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Vitiligo
rejected.why: Vitiligo typically presents with depigmented patches, often with a more irregular shape and distribution, and may be accompanied by other autoimmune symptoms, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Griscelli syndrome
rejected.why: Griscelli syndrome is a rare genetic disorder characterized by albinism, immunodeficiency, and other systemic features, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Nevus of Ito
rejected.why: Nevus of Ito is a congenital condition characterized by a blue-gray pigmentation, typically on the face and neck, which does not match the patient's presentation of hypopigmented macules.

rejected.label: Pityriasis versicolor
rejected.why: The patient was previously treated for tinea versicolor without success, and the presentation of hypopigmented macules without scaling or other characteristic features of pityriasis versicolor makes this diagnosis unlikely.
